title: When is a plane curve projection an immersion?
promptMarkdown: Let $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,\sin2t)$ for $t\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$. Show it is an embedding in $\mathbb R^3$. Compare its projections to the $xy$- and $xz$-planes: determine whether each is injective and whether each is an immersion, and locate all failures.
hintLadder: Use the first two coordinates to recognise the space curve.
A plane derivative vanishes only if both components vanish.
Equality of cosines reduces possible double points to $s=\pm t$.
